S02.title: Local and remote multi-host replication across distinct architectures, mutual TLS with pinned SPKI keys, and canonical membership
S02.evidence: Executed 3-host pilot across owner-desktop (x86_64, Arch Linux), owner-pi (aarch64 Cortex-A72, Debian 12), and main-instance-vnic (aarch64 Neoverse-N1, Ubuntu 24.04). Pinned SPKI TLS 1.3 certificates verified; canonical Revision 1 membership approved.

S03.title: Causal version DAG with vector clocks, concurrent head detection, cryptographic head tokens, and reviewed atomic resolution
S03.evidence: Captured 3 concurrent offline edits across all 3 hosts; gossip produced identical cryptographic head token (087f3db651cb1d0a5bcefa7a8e2da69ff558e6538f9bbaef3958da1f9b3cf286) on all nodes without silent overwrite. Reviewed resolution committed atomically and converged all 3 replicas to 0 conflicts.

S22.title: Verification across realistic topologies, third-party forwarding, resumption, restore, and benchmark matrix against full-file baseline
S22.evidence: Verified A -> VPS -> B forwarding with Host A offline; multi-chunk 3 MiB transfer verified; forward historical restore verified without DAG rollback. Benchmarks demonstrated 97.5% - 99.99% wire savings on tail edits and renames, while documenting the negative result of 1-byte prefix shift defeating fixed 1 MiB chunking.

small_files_1000.bottleneck: Metadata and IOPS bound (~350B per envelope, per-file SQLite records)

unchanged_tree_rescan.bottleneck: Stat-cache verification short-circuits chunk transfer (0 payload bytes transferred)

large_file_tail_edit_40mb.bottleneck: Disk chunk seek; 39 of 40 chunks reused from local object store

prefix_insertion_1byte_shift_20mb.bottleneck: Fixed 1 MiB chunk boundaries shifted by 1 byte; 100% chunk retransmission

file_rename_40mb.bottleneck: Envelope metadata transfer only; 100% chunk reuse from local store
